note: Where somebody stands with a translation, on four questions that are independent — has it been published and by whom, which way it drifted, under whose name the screen acts, what it is in its lineage — composed ONCE from the facts every screen already holds. The mod's main screen used to read the same facts twice (a layout state, then a Standing rebuilt from that state) and the two disagreed: the chip for a vanished Main never appeared in a game. The role is only ever this account's: an answer from the public endpoint says nothing about a person, so a role is taken only when the reader owns a row.

in.lines: int: how many lines the file holds
in.local_changes: int: lines changed since the last sync
in.metadata_dirty: bool: the file's settings changed since the last sync
in.last_synced: the server content last agreed with, absent for a file that never synced
in.checked: bool: the server has been asked at all
in.exists: bool: something of this lineage is on the site
in.is_owner: bool: the reader holds a row in the lineage
in.role: Main | Branch | Fork | None — meaningful only with is_owner
in.uploader: who published the row the server described
in.main_username: who leads the lineage, when the server names them apart
in.branches_count: int: contributions on this Main, whatever their state
in.branches_with_work: int or absent: how many of them hold something to merge
in.lines_available: int or absent: distinct lines those contributions hold

from.out: {publication, sync, account, role, branches_waiting, lines_available, main_missing, main_abandoned, branch_frozen, finished, main_owner} — compared on the keys the case names

leads_the_lineage.out: bool: this account leads the lineage — a Main, or a Fork, which is a Main

on_a_branch.out: bool: this account holds a contribution to somebody else's Main

explain_refusal.out: the sentence with the way out, empty when nothing is refused

cases.why: no file on this machine is the first question, whatever the site holds; who leads it is still worth naming
nothing published to compare against is not 'in sync': it is no comparison at all, so the sync is absent rather than a verdict
what is WAITING, not how many people contribute: two of the three hold nothing a merge would offer
unknown is not zero: telling a Main their contributions are settled when nobody knows is a claim, the raw count is not
a Fork IS a Main: it reviews contributions like one
the lineage's count is its Main's business; carried over, it would send a branch author to review other people's work
holding a community translation without having sent anything: not a Branch, and the person most likely to press a button expecting to create their own
the row the server described may be a branch's; who LEADS the lineage is the person to name
🔴 the public endpoint answers about a translation, never about a person: its role is what an anonymous caller can be told, and a signed-out reader was shown the owner's buttons on it
the direction is kept: which side moved decides whether to take an update or to publish
the verdict is the socle's Sync.Decide on the same four facts every product reads
identical content is in sync whatever the counters say — Sync.Decide asks that first; a changed setting alone does not make an upload
somebody with no account can hold a community translation and diverge from it; the account decides which acts are offered, never what they may know
🔴 the field the main screen never filled, so the chip for a vanished Main never appeared in a game while the notice beside it did
nothing inside the game changes when a Main closes: unless a screen says it, the discovery happens at the moment of publishing
the author's own declaration, which the measurements beside it never answer
an older server, or a lineage nobody asked about: a screen must leave it alone rather than pick one
the state that reviews contributions
a Fork is a Main that left another; judging on the root would demote every fork owner
a branch contributes; it reviews nothing
holding a lineage is not leading it
one becomes a Branch by uploading
somebody holding another's lineage without having sent anything is not a Branch — the distinction the whole NotYours state exists for
merging and re-downloading write nothing but the local file; refusing them an account they do not need tells somebody their work does not count
their own game
not about the server: about not breaking, by inattention, the setup another user of this computer put in place
publishing needs a name
nobody writes on the server without a name
the game's account is not this screen's

cases.out: This game is set up under a different account. To change anything here, open the game and sign in with that account.
cases.why: the way out matters more than the refusal: naming where the account is changed does not leave somebody stuck

cases.out: Sign in to publish. Editing and merging your own copy need no account.
cases.why: the refusal says what still needs no account, so the person is not told their work does not count
empty when nothing is refused
their own account, their own game
